title: ORDERING AT A RESTAURANT
conversation: Tanya: I hope the waiter comes soon. I'm starving! John: Me too! Tanya: Why don't we flag him down? John: Waiter, waiter! Kevin: I'll be right with you! . . . Sorry for the hold up. We're packed to the rafters tonight. John: We noticed! Kevin: I'm Kevin, and I'll be your server tonight. Can I start you off with some drinks? John: I'd like the Sam Adams Summer Ale. Tanya: Make it two. Kevin: And did you decide on some appetizers? John: We're going to skip the appetizers tonight. What do you recommend for a main course? Kevin: We're known for our seafood. The salmon with black bean sauce is our most popular dish. Tanya: Okay, I'll try that. Kevin: Excellent choice. And for you, sir? John: I'm having trouble deciding. I'm in the mood for steak, but I know you pride yourselves on your seafood. Kevin: How about trying the surf and turf? That way, you get the best of both worlds! John: Okay, let's go with that. Kevin: I'll be right back with your drinks. They're on the house because you had to wait so long to order.

idioms.example: I haven't eaten all day, so I'm starving.
idioms.context: I hope the waiter comes soon. I'm starving!
idioms.fill_sentence: I have been working in the garden since six in the morning without taking a single break for breakfast or lunch. My stomach is growling loudly and I feel like I could eat an entire horse right now. I'm starving, so please tell me that dinner is almost ready.

idioms.meaning_en: to get the attention of someone
idioms.meaning_vi: vẫy tay ra hiệu cho ai đó
idioms.example: We need to flag down a taxi if we want to get to the airport on time.
idioms.context: Why don't we flag him down?
idioms.fill_sentence: I was running late for my important job interview and desperately needed a ride. Since there were no buses nearby, I had to stand on the curb and wave my arms to flag down a passing taxi. Thankfully, the driver saw me and pulled over immediately.

idioms.meaning_en: I will help or serve you in a moment
idioms.meaning_vi: Tôi sẽ phục vụ/hỗ trợ bạn ngay đây
idioms.example: Finish your phone call, and I'll be right with you to help with those bags.
idioms.fill_sentence: A customer walks into a busy bakery and approaches the counter while the baker is finishing a large cake order. The baker glances up, smiles at the newcomer, and says, "I'll be right with you" as he puts the final decoration on the cake. He then quickly washes his hands to prepare for the customer's request.

idioms.example: There was a major hold up on the highway due to an accident.
idioms.fill_sentence: We were supposed to start the important meeting at nine o'clock sharp. However, a technical issue with the projector caused a major hold up, so we had to wait twenty minutes for the IT staff to fix it.

idioms.meaning_vi: chật kín người, không còn chỗ trống
idioms.example: The stadium was packed to the rafters for the final game of the season.
idioms.context: We're packed to the rafters tonight.
idioms.fill_sentence: We arrived at the concert venue ten minutes before the show started. Every seat and standing area was already packed to the rafters with excited fans. There was simply no room left for anyone else to squeeze in.

idioms.idiom: Can I start you off with
idioms.meaning_en: a phrase used by servers to ask for an initial order (usually drinks or appetizers)
idioms.meaning_vi: Tôi có thể bắt đầu phục vụ bạn món... không?
idioms.example: Can I start you off with some fresh bread and water?
idioms.context: Can I start you off with some drinks?
idioms.fill_sentence: After I sat down at the restaurant table, the waiter handed me a menu and pulled out a notepad. He smiled politely and asked, "Can I start you off with something to drink while you look over the food options?" I replied that I would like a glass of iced water before ordering my main course.

idioms.meaning_en: I would like the same thing as the person who just ordered
idioms.meaning_vi: Cho tôi hai phần giống vậy (hoặc cho tôi phần giống người vừa gọi)
idioms.example: If he's having the chocolate cake, make it two!
idioms.fill_sentence: My friend just ordered a large iced latte at the busy cafe counter. I looked at the barista and said, 'Make it two,' because I wanted the exact same drink.

idioms.meaning_en: to choose something after thinking about several possibilities
idioms.example: It took a while, but we finally decided on the blue paint for the kitchen.
idioms.context: And did you decide on some appetizers?
idioms.fill_sentence: We spent three hours looking at all the different university brochures in the library. After carefully comparing the tuition fees and the location of each campus, we finally managed to decide on the best option for my future studies.

idioms.example: I think I'll skip dessert today; I'm too full.
idioms.context: We're going to skip the appetizers tonight.
idioms.fill_sentence: We were in a huge hurry to make it to our movie on time, so we decided to order our main courses immediately. Since the kitchen was very busy, we chose to skip the appetizers to ensure we finished our meal before the trailers started.

idioms.meaning_en: famous for; having a reputation for
idioms.example: This region is known for its beautiful vineyards.
idioms.fill_sentence: My hometown attracts thousands of tourists every single year because of its beautiful beaches. It is widely known for its crystal-clear water and golden sand. People travel from all over the world just to experience this specific scenery.

idioms.meaning_en: to want, to have an appetite for, feeling like doing or having something specific
idioms.meaning_vi: đang muốn/có hứng thú với cái gì
idioms.example: Are you in the mood for Italian food tonight?
idioms.context: I'm in the mood for steak, but I know you pride yourselves on your seafood.
idioms.fill_sentence: I have been working hard all day and now I finally have a break. I am really in the mood for a hot slice of pizza to relax. It sounds like the perfect way to end this exhausting shift.

idioms.meaning_en: to be known for; to be especially proud of something
idioms.meaning_vi: tự hào về điều gì đó của bản thân/cửa hàng mình
idioms.example: They pride themselves on their excellent customer service.
idioms.context: I know you pride yourselves on your seafood.
idioms.fill_sentence: Our local bakery is famous throughout the city for its fresh sourdough bread. The owner likes to pride oneself on using a traditional recipe that has been passed down through three generations. Customers travel from miles away specifically to experience this unique, authentic taste.

idioms.meaning_en: a main course that combines seafood (surf) and meat, usually beef (turf)
idioms.meaning_vi: món ăn kết hợp hải sản và thịt
idioms.example: I couldn't decide between lobster and steak, so I ordered the surf and turf.
idioms.context: How about trying the surf and turf?
idioms.fill_sentence: My parents are celebrating their anniversary tonight and cannot decide between steak or lobster for dinner. To please everyone, they chose a classic surf and turf platter that includes both a juicy filet mignon and a grilled lobster tail. It is the perfect meal for someone who loves both meat and seafood.

idioms.meaning_en: the advantages of two different things at the same time
idioms.meaning_vi: vẹn cả đôi đường, có được cả hai thứ
idioms.example: Living in the suburbs gives her the best of both worlds: peace and quiet, but close to the city.
idioms.context: That way, you get the best of both worlds!
idioms.fill_sentence: I recently decided to work from home three days a week while visiting the office on the other two. By combining the flexibility of remote work with the social benefits of face-to-face meetings, I finally have the best of both worlds. This arrangement allows me to enjoy my home life while still staying connected with my colleagues.

idioms.meaning_en: let's choose that option or make that decision
idioms.meaning_vi: chốt luôn/hãy chọn phương án đó
idioms.example: The red dress looks better on you, let's go with that.
idioms.fill_sentence: After reviewing all three designs for the company logo, the marketing team finally narrowed their search down to the blue one. Since everyone agreed it looked the most professional, the manager said, "I think it is the best fit, so let's go with this option for our final presentation."

idioms.meaning_en: given for free by a business (like a restaurant or bar)
idioms.example: The manager said the drinks are on the house since it's our anniversary.
idioms.context: They're on the house because you had to wait so long to order.
idioms.fill_sentence: We had a wonderful dinner at the restaurant to celebrate our anniversary. When the waiter brought the bill, he told us our bottle of expensive wine was on the house. We were so surprised by this generous gift from the manager.
